source: Sigshell findings about sigscores 40f55c5; reproduce each with `Rscript findings/reproduce.R <id>`

findings.t: `rndsigsub` excludes the wrong genes
findings.b: `randomSignatures` subtracts `getIndex(updateSig(x, i))` from the row numbers, but those are positions inside `i`, not rows of `x`. A signature of k genes therefore removes the first k rows of the matrix. Real signature genes stay in the pool. The roxygen example hides this because its signature is the first 10 rows.
findings.c:
y <- matrix(1:12, nrow = 6, dimnames = list(paste0("g", 1:6), c("S1", "S2")))
table(unlist(randomSignatures(y, i = c("g5", "g6"), n = 200, exclude = TRUE)))
findings.evidence: rows drawn: 3-20 | signature rows 19,20 drawn: TRUE | rows 1,2 drawn: FALSE

findings.t: A constant gene anywhere before the signature corrupts all four GSVA scores
findings.b: `rows = rows[keep]` indexes the signature with a logical vector of one value per gene in the matrix. The positions then point into a smaller matrix. A gene with the same value in every sample (an all-zero gene, for example) changes which genes are scored. This is common in real expression data.
findings.c:
sig <- c("g1", "g3", "g4", "g5")
computeSigScores(x, i = sig, scores = "gsva")
computeSigScores(rbind(gC = c(5, 5, 5), x), i = sig, scores = "gsva")
findings.evidence: without constant gene all 4 equal direct GSVA: TRUE | with it, differ from direct GSVA: gsva,ssgsea,plage,zscore

findings.t: A row with NA moves the GSVA gene set onto different genes
findings.b: `rows = rows[-rmv]` uses positions of removed matrix rows as positions in the signature, and the remaining numbers then point into the shortened matrix. The same kind of mismatch as the constant-gene bug.
findings.c:
y <- x; y[2, 1] <- NA
sigscores:::colEnrichment(y, rows = c(1, 3, 4, 5), method = "zscore")
GSVA::gsva(GSVA::zscoreParam(exprData = y[-2, ], geneSets = list(gs1 = sig)), verbose = FALSE)

findings.t: If GSVA fails, R's printed output stays switched off
findings.b: `sink(nullfile())` runs before GSVA and `sink()` after it, with no `on.exit`. If GSVA errors, `computeScores` catches the error and carries on, and everything printed afterwards in that R session disappears. A shell that wraps this library would be directly affected.
findings.c:
r <- computeSigScores(x, i = sig, scores = c("mean", "zscore"), args = list(zscore = list(minSize = 10)))
sink.number()
findings.evidence: sink depth before 0 after 1 | zscore column all NA: TRUE | line 1710: sink(nullfile())

findings.t: `zStandardisation(by = "cols")` scales incorrectly
findings.b: `sweep(...) / scale` divides a matrix by a vector with one value per column. R recycles down the rows, so each sample's values are divided by a mix of scales. There is no warning.
findings.evidence: max |pkg - scale(x)| by cols: 0.391 | by rows vs t(scale(t(x))): 0

findings.t: `robust = TRUE` standardises a matrix twice
findings.b: The robust branch standardises at lines 659 and 675, and the shared line after it (667 or 683) does it again.
findings.c:
ctr <- matrixStats::rowMedians(x); s <- matrixStats::rowMads(x, center = ctr)
round(zStandardisation(x, robust = TRUE, by = "rows") - (x - ctr) / s, 3)
findings.evidence: equals single standardisation: FALSE | equals applying it twice: TRUE

findings.t: A scorer that fails becomes a column of NA, with no message
findings.b: Each scorer runs inside `tryCatch`, and the handler returns NA for every sample without logging the error. A real failure looks the same as missing data.
findings.evidence: all NA: TRUE | warnings: 0 | messages: 0

findings.t: Two scorers transform after subsetting; the other 16 transform first
findings.b: `trimmedMeanScorer` and `aadScorer` subset to the signature and then transform. The others transform the whole matrix first. With a data-dependent transformer such as quantile normalisation, scores are not comparable across these groups.
findings.c:
q <- getDataTransformer("quantile")
meanScorer(x, i = c(1, 5), transform.fun = q)
trimmedMeanScorer(x, i = c(1, 5), trim = 0, transform.fun = q)
findings.evidence: scorers that subset before transform: trimmedMean,aad | mean: 6.333 6.333 8.5 | trimmedMean trim=0: 7.167 7.167 7.167

findings.t: A data frame input gives a wrong result with no error
findings.b: `computeScores` only accepts a real matrix. A data frame is turned into a list-matrix with one column, every scorer fails, and the failures are hidden. You get one row of NA. `read.csv` returns a data frame, so biologists will hit this.
findings.evidence: rows: 1 | mean: NA | warnings: 0

findings.t: A misspelled score id is dropped with no warning
findings.b: `computeScores` uses `intersect`, so `meen` vanishes. Only if every id is wrong do you get an error. The warning in `getScorers` is never reached from `computeSigScores`.
findings.evidence: columns: sampleID,mean | warnings: 0 | all ids wrong: error

findings.t: An unknown gene becomes an NA row number and disappears under the default `na.rm`
findings.b: `match` gives NA for the unknown gene. With the default `na.rm = TRUE` the score is computed from the other genes, with no message.
findings.evidence: same as without gX: TRUE | warnings: 0 | na.rm=FALSE all NA: TRUE

findings.t: `summation` always errors when `i` is given
findings.b: Line 176 subsets `w`, which doesn't exist in this function. The exported function fails for any `i`.
findings.evidence: result: object 'w' not found

findings.t: `outdir` alone saves nothing, despite `filename` having a default
findings.b: The check uses `missing(filename)`, so the default is never used. You get a warning that says the argument has no default, and the folder is created anyway. The docs say the data will be stored if `outdir` is provided.
findings.c:
d <- file.path(tempdir(), "sigout")
r <- computeSigScores(x, i = sig, scores = "mean", outdir = d)
list.files(d)
findings.evidence: outdir only -> files: 0 | warning: Output directory was provided but 'filename' is missing without default. Data won't be saved. | with filename given: sigscores.rds

findings.t: `computeSE(na.rm = TRUE)` still returns NA
findings.b: `na.rm` only reaches the mean. The sum of squared deviations and `n` still include the NA.
findings.evidence: computeSE(c(1,2,NA), na.rm=TRUE) = NA | sd(c(1,2)) = 0.7071

findings.t: An open connection given to `createLogger` is discarded
findings.b: `openCon` replaces the logger's connection with one opened from `path`. With no path the connection becomes NULL, so nothing reaches yours.
findings.c:
out <- character(); tc <- textConnection("out", "w")
r <- computeSigScores(x, i = sig, scores = "mean", logger = createLogger(con = tc, verbose = FALSE))
close(tc); out
findings.evidence: lines written to given connection: 0 | lines written when path given: 1

findings.t: The exported `gsva`, `ssgsea`, `plage` and `zscore` always return NA
findings.b: They share their names with real scores, but the vector versions are placeholders. The Details section of their documentation does say so.
findings.evidence: NA NA NA NA

findings.t: The default two-sided p-value compares absolute values
findings.b: `abs(rnd) >= abs(obs)` assumes the null distribution is centred at zero. For scores that are always positive it behaves like the one-sided `greater` test. A value far below zero counts as extreme as one far above it.
findings.evidence: ASL(5; -6,4,5,6) = 0.75 (-6 counted as extreme) | on positive values two.sided == greater: TRUE | line 131: 'two.sided' = abs(rnd) >= abs(obs),

findings.t: Random signatures count genes that aren't in the matrix
findings.b: The random set has `length(i)` genes, including unknown ones. The observed score only uses genes that exist, so the two are computed from different numbers of genes.
findings.evidence: signature with 1 known + 1 unknown gene -> random set size 2

findings.t: With one sample, the GSVA scores are always NA
findings.b: With a single column every gene counts as constant, so all genes are removed and the function returns NA.
findings.evidence: colEnrichment: NA | via computeSigScores: NA NA NA NA

findings.t: `cores` above 1 prints foreach's debugging output
findings.b: `forLoop` defaults to `verbose = TRUE` and no caller changes it. In parallel runs, foreach's progress messages are printed.
findings.c: r <- computeSigScores(x, i = sig, scores = "mean", sampling = "permutation", n.repeat = 2, cores = 2)
findings.evidence: lines printed: 14 | first: discovered package(s):

findings.t: There is no seed argument
findings.b: Both draws use R's global random state, in the main process. Call `set.seed` before `computeSigScores` to reproduce a run.
findings.c: set.seed(1); a <- sampleData(x, "permutation", 1); set.seed(1); b <- sampleData(x, "permutation", 1); identical(a, b)
findings.evidence: same seed same draw: TRUE | any seed argument: FALSE | parallel run equals serial run under same seed: TRUE

findings.t: A pool of one gene is treated as `1:n`
findings.b: `sample(x = out, ...)` with a single number draws from 1 to that number, which can include the signature. It only happens when the signature covers all genes but one.
findings.c:
y <- matrix(1:10, nrow = 5, dimnames = list(paste0("g", 1:5), c("S1", "S2")))
randomSignatures(y, i = paste0("g", 1:4), n = 2, exclude = TRUE)
findings.evidence: pool after exclusion: 5 | asked for 4 genes, got: 1,4,5,3

findings.t: `dirExists` creates the folder
findings.b: It also returns whether a path was given, not whether the folder existed. The docs do describe this; the name doesn't.
findings.evidence: returned TRUE | folder now exists: TRUE

findings.t: Custom scorer names are rewritten
findings.b: `data.frame` makes column names syntactically valid, so `my score` becomes `my.score`.
findings.evidence: sampleID,my.score

findings.t: Duplicate sample names are an error
findings.b: They become row names of the result, which must be unique.
findings.c: y <- x; colnames(y) <- c("S1", "S1", "S3"); computeSigScores(y, scores = "mean")
findings.evidence: duplicate row.names: S1

findings.t: IQM is NA for fewer than 4 values
findings.b: Small signatures give NA with no message.

findings.t: Mode ties go to the smallest value
findings.b: `which.max` on a sorted table picks the first maximum. With no repeated values the mode is simply the smallest value.

findings.t: Some numbers come from dependencies' defaults
findings.b: `MAD` multiplies by 1.4826, the default of `stats::mad`. Quartile-based scores use the default quantile type. The GSVA methods use the defaults of `GSVA` 2.0.7, which are shown on `colEnrichment`.
findings.evidence: MAD(1,2,9) = 1.4826 | raw median abs dev = 1 | type arg for quantile in midhinge/iqr: FALSE

findings.t: The docs mention `sampling = "random"`, which doesn't exist
findings.b: The allowed values are none, permutation, bootstrap, rndsig and rndsigsub.
findings.evidence: sampling='random': error | doc line 49: #'If \code{sampling = "random"}, \code{sampling = "bootstrap"},

findings.t: The docs for `stepFunction` reverse `y`
findings.b: The formula gives `y[1]` when x is above the threshold. The code at lines 1911 to 1913 uses `y[1]` when x is below.
findings.evidence: x=1,5,9 thr=5 -> 10,20,30 | doc line 1830: #'y_{1}, \quad \textrm{if} \quad x > threshold \\

findings.t: `transform.sub` is documented but does nothing
findings.b: None of the 18 scorers read it.
findings.evidence: scorers whose body reads transform.sub: 0 of 18

findings.t: The docs describe a `genericScorer` and `computeColMeasures` route that the scorers don't take
findings.b: There is no `genericScorer` function, and the scorers call `matrixStats` or the vector functions directly.
findings.evidence: Rd mentions genericScorer: TRUE | function exists: FALSE | scorers calling computeColMeasures: 0

findings.t: Four scorers reject gene names in `i` when called directly
findings.b: The docs allow names, but `sum`, `mean`, `median` and `mad` pass `i` to `matrixStats`, which only accepts numbers. It works through `computeSigScores`, which converts names first.
findings.evidence: error with gene names: sum,mean,median,mad

findings.t: `getAvailableRandomSamplers` leaves out `none`
findings.b: It is the default in `computeSigScores`.
findings.evidence: listed: permutation,bootstrap,rndsig,rndsigsub | computeSigScores default: none

findings.t: Three setters overwrite the connection instead
findings.b: All three bodies say `object$con = value`. No exported function reaches them.
findings.evidence: after setVerbose(FALSE): verbose = TRUE , con = FALSE | after setLevel('DEBUG'): level = INFO

findings.t: `logAll` never prints
findings.b: `getLogLevels` never includes ALL. No exported function reaches it.
findings.evidence: logAll printed lines: 0 | logInfo printed lines: 1

findings.t: Permutation and bootstrap are random-gene-set nulls, not a measure of score stability
findings.b: The paper (section 2.2) says data sampling evaluates "score stability under data variability". `computeSigScores` reorders whole rows and then restores the row names (lines 309-311), so the signature names land on random rows: permutation scores a random gene set of the same size, exactly like `rndsig`, and bootstrap does the same with replacement. None of them resamples the observed signature's values.
findings.c:
y <- matrix(c(1,10,100,1000,10000, 2,20,200,2000,20000), nrow = 5, dimnames = list(paste0("g",1:5), c("S1","S2")))
set.seed(1); p <- computeSigScores(y, i = c("g1","g2"), scores = "sum", sampling = "permutation", n.repeat = 4000)
set.seed(1); r <- computeSigScores(y, i = c("g1","g2"), scores = "sum", sampling = "rndsig", n.repeat = 4000)
round(rbind(permutation = prop.table(table(p$sum[p$sampleID == "S1"])), rndsig = prop.table(table(r$sum[r$sampleID == "S1"]))), 3)
findings.evidence: permutation and rndsig score the same 10 gene pairs, max frequency difference 0.011 | bootstrap also scores pairs with a repeated gene: TRUE | lines 6-compute-scores.R:309-311: x = x[rnd[[iloop]],,drop=F] rownames(x) = rnames

findings.t: On data without repeated values, mode is the minimum
findings.b: Ties go to the smallest value (finding modal-tie). The vignette's data has no repeated values, so its `mode` column is each sample's lowest signature value; most continuous expression data behaves the same way.
findings.c:
set.seed(5381L, kind = "Mersenne-Twister", normal.kind = "Inversion")
xv <- matrix(sample(1000), nrow = 100, dimnames = list(paste0("g", 1:100), paste0("S", 1:10)))
sv <- rownames(xv)[sample(100, 20)]
identical(computeSigScores(xv, i = sv, scores = "mode")$mode, as.numeric(apply(xv[sv, ], 2, min)))
findings.evidence: vignette data has no repeated values; mode equals the signature minimum in all 10 samples: TRUE

findings.t: A gene listed twice in the signature is counted twice
findings.b: `match` keeps duplicates, so every copy is scored as a separate row. The mean of g1, g3 changes when g1 is listed twice. `updateSig`, which removes duplicates, is not on this path.
findings.c:
computeSigScores(x, i = c("g1", "g3"), scores = "mean")
computeSigScores(x, i = c("g1", "g1", "g3"), scores = "mean")
findings.evidence: mean of g1,g3: 4 3 4.5 | with g1 listed twice: 3.3333 2.3333 5.3333 | R/5-scorers.R:1174: i = match(table = rownames(x), x = i)

findings.t: If two matrix rows share a gene name, only the first is scored
findings.b: `match` returns the first matching row. `read.csv` refuses duplicate row names, but a matrix built in R can have them, and nothing warns.
findings.c:
y <- x; rownames(y)[2] <- "g1"
computeSigScores(y, i = c("g1", "g3"), scores = "mean")
findings.evidence: matrix rows 1 and 2 are both g1; scoring g1,g3 uses only the first g1 row: TRUE | no warning

findings.t: Quantile normalisation drops rows with NA, so scorers index the wrong rows
findings.b: With the default `na.rm = TRUE`, `quantileNormalizationForMatrix` removes rows containing NA (line 230). Scorers then apply the original row numbers to the shorter matrix: the signature lands on different genes or out of range, and the scores become wrong or NA without a message.
findings.c:
y <- x; y[2, 1] <- NA
q <- getDataTransformer("quantile")
computeSigScores(y, i = c("g4", "g5"), scores = "mean", args = list(mean = list(transform.fun = q)))
colMeans(q(y)[c("g4", "g5"), ])
findings.evidence: after quantile normalisation the matrix has 4 rows (g2 dropped by R/4-data-preprocessing.R:230); mean of g4,g5: NA NA NA | correct values: 9.5 9.5 8 | warnings: 0
